extracted.intended_audience: Banks and other insured depository institutions, bank compliance officers and legal counsel, federal banking agency staff, and stakeholders interested in CRA implementation (e.g., community groups, industry associations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements implementing the agencies' supplemental rule to the 2023 Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) Final Rule, including interim final rule applicability dates, facility-based assessment area delineation, public file and public notice requirements, performance tests, technical amendments, and procedural instructions for submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRA statutory assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRA requires the agencies to assess a bank's record of meeting the credit needs of its entire community, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods, consistent with the bank's safe and sound operation; upon completing this assessment, the statute requires the agencies to 'prepare a written evaluation of the institution's record of meeting the credit needs of its entire community, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.' The statute further provides that each agency must consider a bank's CRA performance 'in its evaluation of an application for a deposit facility by such institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory mandate that frames all CRA regulations and evaluations. Agencies implement the CRA and establish the framework and criteria by which they assess a bank's performance through their individual CRA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility-based assessment areas (Section __.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.16 provides that a bank must delineate one or more facility-based assessment areas within which the agencies evaluate the bank's record of helping to meet the credit needs of its entire community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section __.16 prescribes the types of deposit-taking facilities that trigger the requirement, the geographic requirements of a facility-based assessment area (e.g., each facility-based assessment area must consist of a single metropolitan statistical area (MSA), one or more contiguous counties within an MSA, or one or more contiguous counties within the nonmetropolitan area of a State (§__.16(b)(2))). §__.16(b)(3) permits intermediate banks or small banks to adjust boundaries to include only the portion of a county the bank reasonably can be expected to serve, subject to the requirement that such a facility-based assessment area consist of contiguous whole-census tracts and comply with limitations in §__.16(c). Section __.16(c) provides that facility-based assessment areas may not reflect illegal discrimination and may not arbitrarily exclude low- or moderate-income census tracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public file content and availability (Section __.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.43 requires a bank to maintain a public file, in either paper or digital format, that includes specific information related to the bank's branches, services, and performance in helping meet community credit needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision largely retains legacy public file requirements with clarifications and revised terminology. Key elements: (1) banks with a public website must include their CRA public file on the website; (2) banks without a public website must maintain public file information at the main office and, if interstate, at one branch in each State; (3) under legacy regs, the public file must be available for public inspection upon request at no cost at main office and (for interstate banks) at one branch office in each State; (4) the 2023 Final Rule clarified 'current year' items and requires quarterly updates for the prior quarter by March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 for items such as written comments and branch openings/closings (§__.43(a)(1) and (a)(4)). The supplemental rule moves the applicability date of §__.43 to January 1, 2026 to align with other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability date alignment for facility-based assessment areas and public file
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies adopt an interim final rule extending the applicability date of the facility-based assessment areas provision (§__.16) and the public file provision (§__.43) from April 1, 2024, to January 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: §__.16 and §__.43 reference provisions and terms (e.g., definitions in §__.12, performance tests and strategic plan in §__.21) that do not apply until January 1, 2026; asset-size thresholds and bank classifications differ between the transition period and post-transition period; aligning applicability dates promotes stability and avoids evaluating banks under different delineation standards within a single year. Agencies request comment on these applicability-date changes (comments due May 13, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice requirement and CRA Notice (Section __.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.44 requires a bank to provide a CRA Notice in the public area of its main office and each of its branches, as set forth in appendix F, that includes information about the availability of a bank's public file, the appropriate Federal financial supervisory agency's CRA examination schedule, and how a member of the public may provide public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The posting requirement is substantively the same as longstanding legacy public notice requirements. Because appendix F (the 2023 Final Rule CRA Notice) is not applicable until January 1, 2026, agencies amended §__.51(a)(2)(i) so banks may continue to use the CRA Notice in the agencies' legacy CRA regulations (as reproduced in appendix G) until January 1, 2026. The amendment to move applicability of §__.44 to January 1, 2026 has no substantive effect but clarifies intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance tests and evaluation framework (Sections __.21, __.22-___.26, __.29-___.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2023 CRA Final Rule establishes performance tests and an evaluation framework (e.g., Retail Lending Test (§__.22), Retail Services and Products Test (§__.23), Community Development Financing Test (§__.24), Community Development Services Test (§__.25), provisions for limited-purpose banks (§__.26), small bank performance evaluation (§__.29), and intermediate bank performance evaluation (§__.30)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These performance tests and related evaluation provisions are applicable as of January 1, 2026. They determine how CRA activities qualify for consideration, where activities are considered (assessment areas), and how activities are evaluated. The facility-based assessment area applicability was aligned with these tests to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic plan evaluation (Section __.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The strategic plan provision (§__.27) allows for evaluation of an insured depository institution on the basis of a strategic plan and identifies elements of such a plan (e.g., §__.27(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies adopted a technical amendment to correct a missing conforming amendment in the strategic plan provision (changing text to 'Operating subsidiaries' or 'Operation subsidiaries' as appropriate). When evaluated under a strategic plan, any element of the strategic plan described in the relevant provision is considered CRA-eligible activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-size thresholds and bank classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies' legacy CRA regulations and the 2023 CRA Final Rule define bank size categories (e.g., small bank, intermediate small bank, intermediate bank, large bank) that determine which rules and tests apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix G and agency updates reflect annual inflation adjustments. The updated asset-size thresholds noted in the supplemental rule: small bank = less than $1.564 billion as of December 31 of either of the prior two calendar years; intermediate small bank = at least $391 million as of December 31 of both of the prior two calendar years and less than $1.564 billion as of December 31 of either of the prior two calendar years. Classification affects whether a bank must delineate full counties versus partial counties for facility-based assessment areas and which performance tests apply during transition/post-transition periods. The Board and FDIC updated appendix G to reflect these thresholds; the OCC issues a Bulletin for its annual threshold announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition provision and use of legacy regulations (Section __.51 and Appendix G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.51 and appendix G explain transition rules and list which provisions of the 2023 CRA Final Rule apply as of different dates (e.g., April 1, 2024; January 1, 2026; January 1, 2027) and reproduce legacy CRA regulations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments clarify that for provisions not applicable until after April 1, 2024, banks must comply with relevant provisions of legacy CRA regulations set forth in appendix G until the later applicability dates. The agencies amended §__.51(a)(2)(i) to align applicability dates for certain provisions (e.g., §__.44) with the CRA Notice in appendix F.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRA Sunshine regulations — disclosure and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRA Sunshine statute and implementing regulations require nongovernmental entities or persons, insured depository institutions, and affiliates that are parties to certain agreements in fulfillment of the CRA to make the agreements available to the public and the appropriate agency and to file annual reports concerning the agreements with the appropriate agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental rule updates cross-references in the CRA Sunshine regulations (12 CFR parts 35 (OCC), 207 (Regulation G) (Board), and 346 (FDIC)) to conform with changes made by the 2023 CRA Final Rule. Agencies reaffirm the types of activities that 'fulfill the CRA' for purposes of these disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities given favorable CRA consideration (Section 346.4(a)(2) / appendix G cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing any of the following activities if the activity is of the type that is likely to receive favorable consideration by a Federal banking agency in evaluating CRA performance: (i) Home-purchase, home-improvement, small business, small farm, community development, and consumer lending; (ii) Making investments, deposits, or grants, or acquiring membership shares, that have as their primary purpose community development; (iii) Delivering retail banking services; (iv) Providing community development services; (v) For wholesale or limited-purpose institutions, community development lending, qualified investments, or community development services; (vi) For small institutions, any lending or other activity described in §345.26(a); (vii) For institutions evaluated on the basis of a strategic plan, any element of the strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerated list (as revised in §346.4) cross-references appendix G to 12 CFR part 345 for definitions and descriptions. It is used to determine whether an activity in a CRA-related agreement is of a type likely to receive favorable consideration and therefore triggers Sunshine filing/disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on illegal discrimination and arbitrary exclusion in assessment-area delineation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.16(c) provides that facility-based assessment areas may not reflect illegal discrimination and may not arbitrarily exclude low- or moderate-income census tracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When delineating facility-based assessment areas, banks must ensure boundaries do not discriminate or exclude LMI tracts arbitrarily; see §__.16(c)(1) and (2) for the explicit limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission procedures and disclosure of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies provide specific instructions for submitting comments (e.g., via Regulations.gov using Docket ID OCC-2022-0002; Board submission methods including agency website, email regs.comments@federalreserve.gov, fax, mail; FDIC email comments@fdic.gov, mail, hand-delivery), require use of docket/RIN numbers, and note that comments will be entered into the docket and published on relevant agency websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies encourage use of the Federal eRulemaking Portal and provide help contacts. The OCC and Board note that comments will be published without change (including contact information); FDIC may redact or refrain from posting inappropriate material and may post a representative example of identical comments. Commenters are advised not to include confidential or inappropriate information. Comments received, including attachments, become part of the public record and are subject to disclosure under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public file update schedule and 'current year' clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2023 CRA Final Rule clarified the meaning of 'current year' for public file requirements (e.g., all written comments received from the public for the current year and the prior two calendar years related to the bank's performance; list of branches opened or closed during the current year and each of the prior two calendar years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clarification requires updates to the public file 'on a quarterly basis for the prior quarter by March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31.' This schedule applies to items the rule identifies as tied to the 'current year' and prior two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer loan disclosure in the public file (exception and interaction with performance tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section __.43 of the 2023 CRA Final Rule does not require disclosure of consumer loan information in the public file because most consumer loans will be considered qualitatively under the Retail Services and Products Test (§__.23), with the exception of automobile loans for certain banks as specified in the Retail Lending Test (§__.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Retail Services and Products and Retail Lending Tests are not applicable until January 1, 2026, the agencies aligned the applicability date of §__.43 with the performance tests to ensure consistency in public file requirements concerning consumer loans during the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical amendments and conforming cross-reference changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies are making a set of technical amendments to the 2023 CRA Final Rule and related regulations that do not change the substance or meaning of the rule, including correcting cross-references, fixing amendatory instruction errors, and updating language (e.g., replacing 'the Federal Reserve' with 'the Board', correcting 'Operations subsidiaries or operating subsidiaries' to agency-specific text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: amending §__.51(a)(2)(i) to align applicability dates; correcting cross-references in appendix B (Calculations for the Community Development Tests); updating appendices G in parts 25, 228, and 345 to reflect updated asset-size thresholds; conforming CRA Sunshine regulations and OCC Public Welfare Investment regulation cross-references to the new CRA rule structure. These amendments are non-substantive but necessary for operability and clarity.
